newsitem.title: USA: NYCE cotton ends sharply down, trade a late seller.
newsitem.headline: NYCE cotton ends sharply down, trade a late seller.

text.p: NYCE cotton futures closed weaker for the sixth consecutive day as late-session trade selling pressured the front months to new contract lows, dealers said.
March cotton settled down 1.45 cents at 71.65 cents per pound, traded 73.70 to 70.85 cents, a life-of-contract low. May ended down 1.76 to 73.09 after hitting a contract low of 73.00.
Volume was estimated at a brisk 22,000 lots compared to Friday's official volume of 8,464 lots.
Sharon Johnson, an analyst with Frank Schneider and Co Inc, said the large open interest in March with five days remaining until first notice day, put pressure on the market.
"Open interest in unusually high and with certificated stocks up to 144,155, the longs were the ones most likely to feel the heat," she said
Open interest in March fell 871 lots to 15,061 lots as of Friday's close.
Cotton prices climbed higher early on mostly speculative and fund buying, but trade selling with about an hour left on the clock pushed prices through stops and ultimately to new contract lows.
Market sources expect brisk mill buying overnight which will appear in next Thursday's export and sales report.
